Wenna Marrow.narrative: I am a weaver's daughter who married the Reeve's son, and half this town has not forgiven me for it. I keep the Marrow strip beyond the east wall, hoe and sow and carry, and say little in the square because whatever I say is repeated. My mother will not sell cloth to this house, and the child coming will be born into that silence. Still, I chose Tobin and I would choose him again.
values: my mother, though she shames me
goals: bring the child safely to birth
make the Marrow strip feed the household well
mend something with my mother before the baby comes
learn to weave a fine winter cloth well enough to sell at the square on its own merit
keep a small garden of her own herbs by the door for the child and the house

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He stood by me when the whole square was talking; I will not let him down.

relations.name: Aldith Weaver
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She means well, but her grudge feeds the very talk she hates.

relations.name: Leofwine Weaver
relations.label: father
relations.note: He says nothing and that is a kindness.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: The Reeve is courteous to me and I am never sure it is not a weighing.

relations.name: Cuth Marrow
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She keeps a quiet house and asks no questions, which I count a mercy.

relations.name: Maud Marrow
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the gate ledger and watches me as if I were a column that might not add up.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: She has delivered half the town and will deliver mine; I trust her hands.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: the other woman
relations.note: I have never met her and I think of her more than I should.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: The inn cook has been kind to me over the counter, and says less than most.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: the wronged father
relations.note: He thinks my marriage was an insult to his house; I have never spoken to him, and I doubt he has ever said my name.

memories.gist: Tobin came to my father's loom-shed and asked for me before he had told his own father; I said yes before he finished.
The morning after the wedding, women in the square stopped their talk as I passed and started it again behind me.
My mother told me she would not sell cloth to the Marrow house, and not to ask her again; my father looked at the floor.
The Lean Year: the berry blight reached our field and we ate from the town store like everyone, and I learned what a ledger's kindness costs.
Joan Hobson put her hand on my belly and said the child was well set; I cried in the lane after she had gone.
I stood at the east gate and watched a Kettlebridge cart pay the due, and knew the carter's look was for me.

stances.why: Whatever I say is repeated and turned; silence is the only cloth that does not fray.
I will not be a mouth the Reeve's ledger has to carry.
He chose me when it cost him, and I will not make him regret it.
Her anger is for me, however it lands; I will not hate her for it, but I will not obey it either.
Everything else can wait; this one thing cannot.

Wenna Marrow.secret: I have written a letter to Hester Crane and burned it twice, and I keep the third unsent in the loom-chest. I want to know what she is like, and I am ashamed of wanting it.
pastimes: walking the Marrow strip at dusk, checking the rows and pulling a weed or two on the way
spinning yarn on her mother's old wheel, the one thing Aldith let her take
sitting with Joan Hobson over a cup of something warm, listening to her talk of births
Wenna Marrow.calling: I would have a loom of my own and cloth that folk buy for its weave, not for my name or my shame.

Tobin Marrow.narrative: I am the Reeve's son and captain of the gate guards, and I broke a promise to a Kettlebridge foundry's daughter because I would not marry where I did not love. The town has not let me forget it and Kettlebridge has not either. My father is old and has named no heir, and the square is split between him and Mercy Abbot over the due that pays my men. I will not see the guards unpaid, and I will not hear my wife slighted.
values: my word given freely, not sold
goals: keep the gate-due so the guards are paid
clear the Coldwell outlaws from the stone road
see Wenna brought to bed safely
settle what comes after my father, in time
train a younger guard up to keep the watch as he does, so the gate is not all on him
own a good horse of his own, bought with his own marks

relations.name: Wenna Marrow
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She is the reason I broke the match and the reason I do not regret it.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is old and will not say who follows him, and I will not ask twice.

relations.name: Cuth Marrow
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She says little and sees everything, and she has never once blamed Wenna.

relations.name: Maud Marrow
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She keeps the gate ledger better than I could, and I would trust her with it.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She would drop the due and leave my guards to beg; I will not have it.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: the promise I broke
relations.note: I did her a wrong and I know it, but I will not be lectured by her father's town.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: He sends our stone south out of spite and calls it the market; let him.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: my guard
relations.note: He takes the due at the south gate and does not flinch from the carters.

relations.name: Aldith Weaver
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She will not forgive the match and says so in the square, and Wenna pays for it.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: Her people have robbed carts on my road twice; the road must be cleared.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: the chapel
relations.note: She heals outlaws and disapproves of the due, and I respect her anyway.

relations.name: Walter Stanhope
relations.label: my guard
relations.note: A short temper and a good arm at the south gate; I would not lose him.

relations.name: Leofwine Weaver
relations.label: wife's father
relations.note: He says nothing to my face, which is more than his wife gives me, and I take that as the peace it is.

memories.gist: A month before the wedding I told Josiah Crane in his own foundry yard that I would not marry Hester, and he did not raise his voice, which was worse.
I married Wenna in the chapel with half the square watching and my father's face like a shut door.
The Lean Year: I stood at the gate while the Coldwell farmers were turned away with their fields gone, and I said nothing because it was my father's doing.
Silas Pike came in with his cart cut open and his berries taken; I promised him the road would be cleared and it has not been.
I found Wenna crying in the lane after the market and could not get from her who had spoken; I wanted to hit someone and there was no one to hit.
My father showed me the gate ledger and said the due pays the men who keep the wolves off the road, and that was all the explaining he ever did.

stances.why: It pays the guards who keep the road clear; drop it and the wolves and the outlaws come through the gate.
Carters are robbed on my road and I gave my word it would stop.
I would not marry where I did not love, and no one will make me sorry for it.
They priced their stone high and send it south out of spite; I will not crawl to them for peace.
The guards answer to me, and a captain who cannot pay them is no captain.

Tobin Marrow.secret: I have begun to wonder whether my father will ever name me after him, and whether Mercy Abbot will be Reeve before I am; I have said this to no one, not even Wenna.
pastimes: walking the gate road at first light with Wat Fenner, checking the ruts and the wolf sign
throwing dice at the inn when the watch is done, though he loses more than he wins
riding out to the Coldwell woods edge to look at the fields he means to see cleared
Tobin Marrow.calling: I am a captain of the gate and I would keep the road clear and my men paid; that is work worth doing, and I do it well.
